- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- If model shows sharp upward spike after a recent dip, it often overshoots — cap forecast at +3–5% above prior high or adjust downward 2–3 days later.
- In low-sentiment periods (avg sentiment < -0.2), model frequently underestimates true price — add 2–4% to forecast mean for 3–5 day horizon.
- When sentiment is neutral or slightly positive (avg 0.0–0.3), model often underreacts to true price momentum — increase forecast slope by 1–2% per day.
- If model forecast is consistently below true outcome for 3+ consecutive days, apply mean reversion: adjust forecast to 1.5–2x the 10-day moving average of true values.
- For 30-day horizon, if model shows strong upward trend but sentiment is weak, reduce forecast by 3–5% to avoid overconfidence bias.
- If sentiment turns positive after a negative streak, model often lags — delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days and add 1–2% upward bias.
- In high-sentiment periods (avg > 0.3), model tends to overestimate — cap forecast at 10% below recent high or adjust downward 1–2 days after spike.
